Nakayama Steel Works Ltd Announces Major Plant Expansion in Osaka Prefecture

Osaka—Nakayama Steel Works Ltd, a key player in Japan's steel manufacturing sector, has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its production facility in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture. The company announced on Thursday that it will invest approximately ¥12 billion over the next three years to upgrade and enlarge its rolling mill operations, aiming to boost output capacity and strengthen its position in the domestic and regional markets.

The expansion, which is scheduled to begin later this year, will see the installation of state-of-the-art rolling equipment, automated quality control systems, and enhanced environmental measures. According to Nakayama Steel Works Ltd, the improvements are expected to increase annual production by 180,000 metric tons, primarily serving the construction, automotive, and machinery sectors.

“We are committed to supporting the ongoing growth of Osaka’s manufacturing base and meeting the evolving needs of our customers,” said President Hiroshi Kawaguchi at a press conference. “This investment will not only improve efficiency and product quality, but also contribute to lower emissions and energy consumption in line with our sustainability goals.”

The project is anticipated to create around 60 new jobs at the Sakai site, adding to the company’s current workforce of 850 in the region. Local officials have welcomed the news, highlighting the potential for economic revitalization.

“Osaka has a proud industrial heritage, and this expansion by Nakayama Steel Works Ltd is a testament to the strength of our manufacturing sector,” said Sakai City Mayor Yumi Takamura. “We look forward to continued collaboration and the positive impact this will have on employment and local businesses.”

Industry observers note that the move comes as demand for high-quality steel products remains stable, particularly in the Kansai region, where infrastructure and urban redevelopment projects are ongoing. Takehiro Matsuda, a steel industry analyst at the Kansai Metal Federation, commented, “Nakayama’s decision reflects both confidence in future market conditions and a proactive approach to technological innovation. Investments like these are vital for keeping Japan’s steel sector competitive.”

The Osaka Chamber of Commerce also expressed its support. “The project will stimulate local supply chains and offer new opportunities for small and medium enterprises,” said spokesperson Eri Sakamoto.

Construction on the expanded facilities is expected to begin in September, with completion targeted for late 2026. Nakayama Steel Works Ltd confirmed that it will work closely with local contractors and suppliers throughout the process, ensuring that the bulk of procurement and labor benefits the surrounding community. The company further reaffirmed its commitment to environmental responsibility, noting that the new systems will help reduce water usage and industrial waste.

The announcement marks the largest single investment by Nakayama Steel Works Ltd in over a decade, underscoring its long-term commitment to the Osaka region and the Japanese steel industry.
